title: Peninsula Healthcare QBR narrative draft - renewal prep
content:
Context and goal:
- Audience: Peninsula Healthcare execs (CTO: Dana Ruiz, Head of AI: Ravi Shah), product owners (Clinical Search) and infra leads.
- Objective for this QBR: 1) demonstrate realized value since deployment (last 6 months), 2) align on renewal in May, 3) get buy-in for a Dedicated evaluation pilot (3 months) to reduce cost and improve p99 latency.
- Tone: consultative, numbers-first, surface FRs and risk mitigation. Keep ask concrete.

One-line narrative (elevator):
- "Peninsula has migrated clinician-facing search to Redwood-hosted v2 models and achieved a 45% reduction in average lookup time and 18% fewer escalations to clinical ops — next step is a Dedicated pilot to secure predictable latency and save ~28% per-token cost at scale."

High-level slide flow (10–12 slides) + speaker notes (working):
1) Title / meeting goals (30s)
   - Note: name attendees, confirm 60 minutes + 15 for Qs.

2) Where we started (30s)
   - Deployment snapshot at kickoff (Sept 2025): hosted Llama-2-70B-reduced, pilot traffic 30k qpm.
   - Risks we tracked then: cold-start p99 spikes, data residency concerns for a subset of clinics.

3) What happened since (2–3 minutes) — headline metrics (one-liner + bullets)
   - Usage growth: from 30k qpm -> 110k qpm peak; avg monthly tokens: 1.2B -> 4.6B
   - Latency: median token latency improved 37% after KV caching and prompt prefixing; p99 improved from 740ms -> 410ms for service routes.
   - Cost/unit: per-1000-token spent down ~12% after our batching recommendations.
   - Clinical ops impact: escalations (manual overrides) dropped 18% (measured via support tickets).
   - Speaker note: call out specific clinic example where search suggestions prevented erroneous triage.

4) Demo or screenshot (1 minute)
   - Quick playback of a clinician flow with TTL caching; show telemetry traces (console screenshots).
   - Speaker note: keep under 60s. We can omit if execs prefer numbers.

5) Reliability and incidents (1 minute)
   - 3 incidents since rollout: two transient p99 spikes (service autoscaling misconfig at midnight), one model mismatch regression (rollback done in 2 hours).
   - MTTx: mean time to mitigation averaged 45 minutes; post-incident runbook reduced that to 22 minutes in last month.
   - Action: we recommend weekly smoke tests and add a canary route for new model uploads.

6) Health / risk quadrant (1 minute)
   - Health score: 78/100 (usage + latency + incidents + adoption).
   - Renewal risk: MEDIUM (reasons: budget cycle in May, increased vendor scrutiny, some latency-sensitive clinics).

7) Strategic wins & customer quotes (1 minute)
   - Quote: "Search latency improvement prevented several misclassifications during peak hours" — Dr. Mei Tran, Peninsula ED.
   - Use-case wins: triage suggestions, note summarization pilot (20% time savings for clinicians).

8) Opportunity map and asks (2 minutes)
   - Near-term asks (this QBR): secure 3-month Dedicated pilot for 4x GPUs (target start June), commit to a renewal conversation week of May 4th.
   - Upsell potential: Dedicated + Optimize subscription (estimated $xxk ARR) for predictable throughput.

9) Cost/benefit snapshot (2 minutes)
   - Current estimate: hosted monthly avg cost $43k, projected Dedicated pilot cost $31k/mo (28% savings) for comparable latency SLOs.
   - Break-even: ~4 months if usage stable.
   - Speaker note: show simple table: current vs pilot cost, expected p99 impact, ROI.

10) Roadmap alignment (1 minute)
   - Redwood roadmap items relevant: regionized private deploy, token-level billing visibility, advanced KV-expiry control for cache hits.
   - Ask: which of these matter most for Peninsula? (pick top 2).

11) Risks & mitigation plan (1 minute)
   - Data residency: propose Private VPC evaluation for a subset of clinics.
   - Latency SLAs: propose canary + dedicated routing for latency-sensitive endpoints.
   - Model regressions: escalate to weekly evals and prompt regress tests tied to the evaluation harness.

12) Next steps / commitments (1 minute)
   - CS actions: draft Dedicated pilot SOW by Mar 20 (owner: Arjun).
   - Customer actions: decision to pilot by May 1, point-of-contact for infra: Ravi Shah.
   - Follow-up: schedule renewal sync week of Apr 20.

Appendix / backup slides (available if asked)
- Full incident timeline w/ mitigation steps.
- Per-clinic usage breakdown (top 10 clinics by qpm).
- Token-level cost waterfall.
- Example logs showing prefix cache hit-rate improvement (from 12% -> 45%).

Key metrics snapshot (for slide 3) — pull these from telemetry before finalizing: 
- Monthly active clinicians: 2,400 -> target 3,000 by Q3
- Avg session length: 1.7 -> 1.9 queries/session
- Monthly tokens (current rolling 30d): 4.6B
- Median latency (tokens): 48ms -> note: backend vs frontend breakdown
- p99 latency for /search route: 410ms (target for Dedicated pilot: <300ms)
- Support tickets related to inference: 42 in last 90d -> trending down

Renewal playbook (working checklist)
- 12 weeks before renewal (Mar 1): schedule QBR and send pre-read (owner: CS AE).
- 8 weeks: share usage + cost analysis + proposed pilot SOW.
- 4 weeks: finalize pilot scope, sign-off on data residency terms.
- 2 weeks: confirm seats, technical dry-run, and access for Dedicated (if approved).
- Decision week (May): negotiate contract; recommended T&Cs: pilot discount, rollback clause, observability retention 90d.

Negotiation levers (notes for internal team)
- Give pilot pricing concession in exchange for a 12-month renewal commitment if pilot meets p99 SLA.
- Offer uplift credits for migrating non-critical workloads to Dedicated within 90 days.
- Keep BAA + SOC2 scoping as a separate SOW to avoid contract delays.

Open questions / TODOs (internal)
- Confirm exact monthly token baseline with billing (Action: Liam, due 2026-03-12).
- Pull per-route p99 histograms for last 6 weeks (Action: Maya, due 2026-03-10).
- Draft SOW template w/ pilot KPIs and rollback clause (Action: Arjun, due 2026-03-20).
- Ask legal to pre-vet data residency clause, esp around PHI (Sofia).

Notes-to-self / presentation tips:
- Keep the first 3 slides tight — execs want headline metrics and the ask up front.
- Use a single slide to show "what success looks like" for Peninsula: p99 <300ms, -25% monthly inference cost, zero regressive outputs on the QA prompt set.
- Bring one success story from another healthcare customer for credibility, but avoid direct comparables that expose pricing.
- Prepare a short 90-second demo script in case they ask for a live run.

References / links to artifacts to populate final slides:
- Confluence: Peninsula Health onboarding (linked above)
- BI dashboard: internal/cs/dashboards/peninsula-usage (request view if needed)
- Jira: JIRA-2381 (triage escalation), JIRA-2440 (KV cache improvement), JIRA-2502 (latency canary)

Version history (notes):
- 2026-02-28 initial draft (Arjun)
- 2026-03-03 added incident timeline + health score (Maya)
- 2026-03-09 cost snapshot updated; tightened asks (Liam)

Bottom line for the customer (soundbite for slide 2):
- "We’ve delivered measurable latency and clinician time savings since rollout. A short Dedicated pilot will secure those gains at lower cost and make latency predictable for your busiest clinics — we’d like a decision to pilot by May so we can align budgets and infra."

-- END DRAFT --
